questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was born and raised in Paris until I turned 9 years old and I have always wanted to go back and try to study in a french-speaking environment and significantly improve my level of french.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Very difficult. I had a meeting with one in the administration about my choice of courses but otherwise I was left on my own. For example the administration could not tell my when the semester started and the process of finding the schedules was very chaotic. The schedule for one of my courses was given half an hour before the course started. On my first day at the university I went to the administration to ask for help to understand how to read the schedule (which was a difficult system to understand) but the staff yelled at me. 
The combination of reciving all information in last minut and the angry staff throughout the semester was quite stressfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Almost nothing. Same as previous question.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was more easy than I expected to be. I lived in the belgium house in Cité Universitaire which is a beautiful park where each nationality has a house where students can live. The place has a lot of great offers such as a cantine, a small theater, very good oppertunities for different kind of sports, a lot of concerts for free... And you get to know people from all over the world. The place is also relatively close to campus. 
I would definitly recommend Cité Universitaire.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find a place close to campus because it takes much longer time to get though Paris than you expect:)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Getting accepted at Sorbonne Université was overall simple. It contained a lot of forms that I had to fill out. I also had to provide the univerity my CV and a motivation letter but I did not have to take a language test even though all the couses are in french.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much. I had a contact person in the administration at Sorbonne but quite often the person didn't reply to my emails. However I didn't really need help in the registration process. It was in the course selection that it started to get more complicated and chaotic.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Overall I couldn't really choose my courses and I wasn't aware of it before I was registered to the university. I had to take the courses that students in biology have to take in 5th semester. One of these courses is an english language course. Because I was an Erasmus student I was not allowed to take english and because I was born in France I was not allowed to take french either but I was still obligated to take a laguage course. 
I was able to change some of the courses in 3th semester instead of 5th semester, but non of them were courses that I really wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't get your hopes to high concerning the choise of courses. It is also very important that you know that the courses are in french.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is comparable to the level at UCPH but at Sorbonne they value the ability to know facts by heart more than the ability to think critically.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
At Sorbonne you don't have any books or papers. You have absolutely nothing to read. The lectures is all you have and these takes 2 hours without any pause. 
Generally there is no self studying instead you have many courses which normally goes from 8.30 in the morning to 18 or 20 in the evening with one break throughout the day which is the lunchbreak. 
They have midterms, assignments and presentations during the semester. The final exames are in the first week of january.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comportement des cellules eucaryotes en conditions physiologiques et pathologique (6 ECTS) 
Mathématiques et statistiques pour la biologie (3 ECTS)
Chinois (3 ECTS)
Neurophysiologie et physiologie des grandes fonctions (6 ECTS)
Microbiologie (3 ECTS)
Les microorganismes pathogènes (6 ECTS)
Orientation Insertion Professionnelle (3 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: To be honest I wouldn't recommend any of the courses. The structure of the courses is generally bad and the professors are not necessarily nice to you or willing to answer your questions.

questions.answer: I had no unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is very cheap in supermarkets and in restaurants. 
Almost all museums are free if you are aged under 26.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different things - but they were usually at the same time as your classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went to the activities at Cité Universitaire and not those at campus because because they were easier to fit into my schedule.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to all the museums you can! They are very large and beautiful. Make sure to visit some of the castles such as Louvre or Versaille they are really extraodinary. And go to a lot of restaurants they are quite nice and cheap:)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Difficult even though I have lived here before. French people are more easily provoked than danes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be intimidated by their temper. Otherwise just be yourself:)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Definitely their temper.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They make delicious food, that you are surrounded by a beautiful language and that the french people value hard work and family life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. I would recommend to have at least C1 level in french - otherwise it is to hard to follow the courses. 
2. I would definitely recommend Paris when going on exchange but not Sorbonne Université if you are studying lifescience (can't tell for the other studies)
3. Be prepared for a lot of bureaucracy

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be sure that you are ready to go through a lot of chaotic situations and to do it in french. 
Do not choose Sorbonne Université if you want to sightsee a lot - the courses have a big workload even without incounting that it is in french.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I improved my french and I came back to Paris just as I wanted:)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Almost everyting at the university.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
